title: Sync Enriched Records to Pipedrive with Cargo: Create, Update or Upsert
summary: Cargo's Pipedrive connector creates, updates and upserts organizations, persons, deals and leads natively. How it matches on the one field you choose, how to make it fail instead of overwriting when several records match, and the cargo-ai commands to run the sync.
body_markdown:
**Yes, Cargo writes enriched go-to-market records back to Pipedrive natively:` upsertRecords` updates the records whose chosen field matches your value and creates one when none does,` updateRecords` only updates, and` insertRecord` only creates.** Update and upsert match on the one field you choose and nothing else, and with` isFailingOnMultipleMatches` turned on they write nothing and fail the row when several records match, instead of overwriting all of them.


## The three write actions#


All three take an` objectType` (` organization` ,` person` ,` deal` or` lead` ) and a list of` mappings` , each a Pipedrive field key and the value to write. Update and upsert also take one` matchingObjectFieldName` and one` matchingValue` .


Action No record matches One record matches Several records match


` insertRecord` Creates one Creates one more Creates one more


` updateRecords` Writes nothing, returns an empty array Updates it Updates every match; with` isFailingOnMultipleMatches` , fails the row instead


` upsertRecords` Creates one, including the matched value; on` id` , fails the row Updates it Updates every match; with` isFailingOnMultipleMatches` , fails the row instead


How the match works:


- **Only the chosen field counts.** Cargo runs Pipedrive’s item search with exact match, restricted to that field where Pipedrive allows it, then checks every hit against the field itself. A record whose value appears in a note or in another field is not a match. The comparison ignores case and surrounding spaces.
- **` id` reads the record instead of searching.** Matching on` id` fetches that one record, so it can never be ambiguous. An id Pipedrive no longer finds, such as a record deleted or merged away, matches nothing:` updateRecords` writes nothing, and` upsertRecords` fails the row with` No organization record found with id 4182` rather than creating a duplicate.
- **A custom field is matched by its key.** Pass the field’s 40-character key (the value the field picker lists for it) as` matchingObjectFieldName` , and only that custom field is compared. The generic` custom_fields` option matches the value in any custom field, so use the key: when nothing matches,` upsertRecords` on the generic option fails the row unless one of your mappings writes the value into a custom field, because a record created without it would not be found by the next run.
- **Several matches are all updated unless you say otherwise.**` isFailingOnMultipleMatches` is off by default. Turn it on and an ambiguous row writes nothing and fails with an error naming the count, for example` 3 records match the matching value; "Fail on multiple matches" is on, so nothing was written` . There is no option to skip the row silently: a failed row is how the ambiguity reaches you.
- **The matching field is not rewritten on update** unless you map it explicitly.


On create,` upsertRecords` writes every mapping plus the matching value, so the next run finds the record:` name` on organizations and persons,` title` on deals and leads,` address` on organizations,` email` and` phone` on persons (as the primary value), or the custom field whose key you matched on. A value you mapped yourself wins over the matching value.


` skipIfExist` on a mapping writes that field on update only when it is empty in Pipedrive, custom fields included: a custom field key is checked against the stored value under` custom_fields` . On create, every mapping is written.


## Match by id, then domain, then name#


Pipedrive organizations have no domain field you can match on: the searchable organization fields are` name` ,` address` ,` notes` and custom fields. Keep the domain in a custom field, and use the strongest key each row has:


1. **Pipedrive id (` id` ).** If an earlier sync stored the id on your account, update by it with` updateRecords` . It is the only key that cannot be ambiguous.
2. **Domain (your custom field key).** Update on it with` isFailingOnMultipleMatches` on: one match is updated, none returns an empty array, several fail the row.
3. **Name (` name` ).** The weakest key, for rows the domain did not resolve. Same option, same three outcomes.


**Send ambiguous rows to a person.** A row that failed because two organizations share a name is a duplicate in Pipedrive: picking one of them by rule is how a sync writes enrichment onto the wrong account, and merging them is a separate decision. When no key matches anything, create the organization with` upsertRecords` on the domain key, so the new record carries its domain and the next run finds it.


## Run it from the CLI#


Install the CLI, sign in, check the Pipedrive connector, and find the actions. Each result carries the` action` object the commands below take:


shellscript


```text
npm   install   -g   @cargo-ai/cli
cargo-ai   login   --email   you@company.com
cargo-ai   connection   connector   list   --integration-slug   pipedrive
cargo-ai   orchestration   action   list   upsert   --kind   connector   --integration-slug   pipedrive


```


Every record you pass to` execute-batch` is the action’s input. Extra keys, like a` rowId` of your own, are carried through to the results file, which is how you join a result back to the account it belongs to. The examples use` 9f1c2e7a4b3d5f6e8a0b1c2d3e4f5a6b7c8d9e0f` as the key of a custom Domain field; use your own.


**1. Accounts with a Pipedrive id: update by id.**


shellscript


```text
cargo-ai   orchestration   action   execute-batch   \
--action   '{"kind":"connector","integrationSlug":"pipedrive","actionSlug":"updateRecords"}'   \
--records   '[{"objectType":"organization","matchingObjectFieldName":"id","matchingValue":4182,"mappings":[{"propertyName":"9f1c2e7a4b3d5f6e8a0b1c2d3e4f5a6b7c8d9e0f","value":"acme.com"},{"propertyName":"name","value":"Acme","skipIfExist":true}]}]'   \
--wait-until-finished


```


**2. Accounts without an id: update by domain, failing on duplicates.**


shellscript


```text
cargo-ai   orchestration   action   execute-batch   \
--records   '[{"rowId":"acc_1","objectType":"organization","matchingObjectFieldName":"9f1c2e7a4b3d5f6e8a0b1c2d3e4f5a6b7c8d9e0f","matchingValue":"acme.com","isFailingOnMultipleMatches":true,"mappings":[{"propertyName":"name","value":"Acme","skipIfExist":true}]}]'   \
--wait-until-finished


cargo-ai   orchestration   batch   download   --uuid   <  batch-uui  d  >


```


` batch download` returns a URL to a CSV with your input columns, including` rowId` , and each row’s result.


**3. Act on each row by what the update did.**


- One record in` data` : done.
- The row failed with “records match the matching value”: skip it and list it for review.
- ` data` is empty: repeat step 2 with` "matchingObjectFieldName":"name"` and the name as` matchingValue` . One match is done, a failure is a skip, and an empty result is a create:


shellscript


```text
cargo-ai   orchestration   action   execute-batch   \
--action   '{"kind":"connector","integrationSlug":"pipedrive","actionSlug":"upsertRecords"}'   \
--records   '[{"objectType":"organization","matchingObjectFieldName":"9f1c2e7a4b3d5f6e8a0b1c2d3e4f5a6b7c8d9e0f","matchingValue":"acme.com","isFailingOnMultipleMatches":true,"mappings":[{"propertyName":"name","value":"Acme"}]}]'   \
--wait-until-finished


```


Pass` --limit 5` to any of these to run a pilot on the first five records and check the result in Pipedrive before the full set.


## What each action returns#


- ` insertRecord` ,` updateRecords` and` upsertRecords` return` data` as an array of the Pipedrive records they wrote, as Pipedrive’s API returns them:` id` and the standard fields, with custom fields of organizations, persons and deals under` custom_fields` , keyed by field key. A create returns one record; an update returns one per record it changed; an update that matched nothing returns an empty array.
- A row stopped by` isFailingOnMultipleMatches` returns no data and fails with the error above. So does an` upsertRecords` row whose` id` no longer exists, or whose generic` custom_fields` match would create a record without the value.


None of the Pipedrive actions carries a credit price. The connector paces its calls to Pipedrive at 5 per second, and each update or upsert makes one search, a read of each candidate record, and one write per match, so a large batch is spread out rather than rejected.


## The limits#


- **An empty` matchingValue` matches nothing.**` updateRecords` then writes nothing, and` upsertRecords` creates a record. Filter out rows with an empty key before the batch.
- **Some matching fields are not written on create.**` notes` on any object, and` email` ,` phone` , organization name and person name on leads, are not a single field Pipedrive takes on create, so a record` upsertRecords` creates on them does not carry the value and the next run creates another. Match on one of the fields listed above, or on a custom field key.
- **The match reads the first 100 search hits.** Hits come from a single Pipedrive item search, capped at one page: a value shared by more records than that is not counted in full, and the row updates at most those 100. The cap is deliberate, so a weak key cannot rewrite hundreds of records in one go. Match on a key that should be unique, and turn` isFailingOnMultipleMatches` on.
- **Each match costs a read.** An update or upsert reads every matching record from Pipedrive before writing it (on a custom field key, every search hit), so a value shared by many records costs one call per record. A key that should be unique keeps that small.


This page covers create, update and upsert. Delete records is a separate action and is not covered here.


## Persons, deals and leads work the same way#


The same actions take` "objectType":"person"` ,` "deal"` or` "lead"` . For persons, match by` id` first, then` email` , and fail what matches twice. To keep the sync running as accounts are enriched, put the same steps in a[play](https://www.getcargo.ai/product/plays) that fires when a record changes, rather than a script on a laptop. The same job on other CRMs is in[sync enriched accounts to HubSpot](https://www.getcargo.ai/blog/sync-enriched-accounts-to-hubspot) ,[sync enriched records to Salesforce](https://www.getcargo.ai/blog/sync-enriched-records-to-salesforce) and[sync enriched accounts to Attio](https://www.getcargo.ai/blog/sync-enriched-accounts-to-attio) . The broader rules for keeping the CRM clean are in[CRM hygiene as code](https://www.getcargo.ai/blog/crm-hygiene-as-code) , and the[CRM enrichment cookbook](https://www.getcargo.ai/cookbooks/crm-enrichment) fills the identifiers this matching depends on.


## Frequently asked questions#


### Can Cargo upsert records in Pipedrive?


Yes. The Pipedrive connector’s` upsertRecords` action updates the records whose chosen field equals your value and creates a record when none does, writing the matched value onto it.` updateRecords` only updates and` insertRecord` only creates.


### What happens when two Pipedrive organizations match?


By default, both are updated. Set` isFailingOnMultipleMatches` to` true` and the row writes nothing and fails with the number of records that matched, so you can send it to a person.


### Does a value in another field count as a match?


No. Update and upsert compare only the field named in` matchingObjectFieldName` . A value that appears in a note or in a different custom field is not a match.


### Can Cargo match Pipedrive organizations by domain?


Only through a custom field. Organizations have no searchable domain field, so store the domain in a custom field and match on that field’s key.


### What happens when I upsert on a Pipedrive id that was deleted?


The row fails with` No organization record found with id` and the id, and nothing is created. A deleted or merged record’s id is not a key a new record can carry, so creating one would only duplicate the account.


### Does syncing to Pipedrive cost Cargo credits?


No. The Pipedrive actions carry no credit price. You need a Pipedrive connector set up with your company domain and an API token.
